data.title: What Dissolves in Water?
data.description: Explore which everyday kitchen items dissolve in water and which ones don't!

substances.name: Table Salt
substances.imagePrompt: A small pile of white table salt crystals

substances.name: Sugar
substances.imagePrompt: A small pile of white sugar granules

substances.name: Sand
substances.imagePrompt: A small pile of brown beach sand

substances.name: Cooking Oil
substances.imagePrompt: Golden cooking oil in a clear glass

separationMethods.description: Pour the mixture through a paper filter to catch solid bits that didn't dissolve.
separationMethods.animation: solid particles get trapped in the paper cone while clear liquid passes through

separationMethods.description: Heat the solution until the water turns to gas and goes into the air, leaving crystals behind.
separationMethods.animation: liquid boils away leaving shiny crystals at the bottom

separationMethods.description: Carefully pour the top liquid layer off the heavier liquid underneath.
separationMethods.animation: top oil layer pours out first leaving water behind

challenges.instruction: Add the sugar to the water and stir. What do you get?
challenges.hint: Look at the beaker after you stir: can you still see the substance, and where is it?
